subject: SummitBridge SDK branching & backport request — API v1 deprecation impact
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Linda Hart <linda.hart@summitbridge.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SummitBridge SDK branching & backport request — API v1 deprecation impact

Hi Linda,

Thanks for the heads up on the API v1 sunset notice you circulated last week. We walked through the note with our integrations team this morning and have a couple of follow-ups before we can finalize the migration plan for customers who rely on the Redwood SDK wrapper for SummitBridge endpoints.

Two specific asks from our side:
- Can SummitBridge publish a short endpoint-usage matrix (which endpoints are changing vs removed) so we can map it against our SDK surface? The attached "sdk-impact-matrix.xlsx" is a first pass from our side — feel free to annotate.
- Would SummitBridge consider maintaining a stable v1-compatible branch (or backport critical auth/serialization fixes) for customers who cannot migrate by May 15? A temporary compatibility branch would reduce churn and give our larger co-sell prospects breathing room.

Operationally we need: an expected hard-deprecation date, a list of any breaking schema changes, and whether there will be token/auth flow adjustments. If SummitBridge can support a short-lived branch, we can reduce the scope of breaking changes in our hosted SDK and push a targeted migration path in two waves.

Can we schedule a 30-minute alignment this week? I propose Thu 4/5 11am PT — I can send a calendar invite if that works.

Thanks — appreciate the partnership on this one.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sdk-impact-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)
From: Linda Hart <linda.hart@summitbridge.io>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kevin Miller <kevin.miller@integral-consulting.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Apr 2028 13:40:00 -0400
Subject: Re: SummitBridge SDK branching & backport request — API v1 deprecation impact

Olga —

Thank you for raising this so clearly and for the spreadsheet; that's helpful. Quick answers up front:
- Hard-deprecation date is May 15, 2028. After that date v1 traffic will be redirected to a compatibility gateway that returns advisory headers for a 90-day window, but we will not guarantee bug fixes on v1 unless explicitly backported.
- Primary breaking changes: request/response envelope normalization for /sessions and /batch/transform, and a token expiration/refresh semantics change (shorter-lived tokens by default). Full list attached in our official notice.

We can support a short-term backport branch for security fixes and the most common serialization edge-cases, but we need a committed scope from Redwood on which endpoints and usage patterns you must keep stable. Kevin (cc'd) is our integrator lead and will coordinate the estimate.

Let's take your proposed Thu 4/5 11am PT — that works for me. I'll send an invite with a short agenda: 1) impact mapping, 2) backport feasibility, 3) timeline & gating.

Best,
Linda Hart
Head of Integrations
SummitBridge

Attachment: summitbridge-api-deprecation-notice.pdf (PDF, 95KB)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SummitBridge SDK branching & backport request — API v1 deprecation impact

Folks —

I reviewed the impact matrix and ran a quick scoping exercise with EngOps. High level:
- The bulk of our customers hit only three endpoints that are changing semantics: /sessions, /batch/transform, and /metrics/push. For those, the work breaks into two streams: (A) compatibility shim in the SDK to translate v1 envelopes to v2 internally (~3 dev-weeks, low-risk), (B) backporting security/refresh token behavior to an SB-maintained v1 branch (~2 dev-weeks on your side + 1 week of joint testing).
- Risk: if SummitBridge does not provide the v1 branch, we can implement the SDK shim but we will still surface behavioral differences (token lifetime, rate-limit headers) to customers. That increases support load and may require offer-level credits for impacted enterprise customers.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm which endpoints SummitBridge will commit to backport (we've highlighted recommended ones in the spreadsheet).
2) If backport is agreed, we open ENG-1298 and attach the backport checklist (link below). Redwood can prioritize a low-risk SDK shim as Plan B.
3) Set an internal go/no-go checkpoint on Apr 20 to finalize customer migration comms.

Estimate: if SummitBridge accepts backport for the three endpoints above, combined effort across both teams is ~6 dev-weeks total; Redwood effort alone for SDK shim fallback is ~3 dev-weeks. Estimated incremental cost: ~$42k implementation + ~$8k testing & rollout.

Link: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/ENG-1298
Attachment: backport-work-estimate.md (markdown, 6KB)

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — quick operational notes:
- Linda: please include the confirmed backport scope in the calendar invite (so Eng can triage pre-meeting).
- Olga: I'll own customer comms cadence and will draft a migration FAQ once we lock the go/no-go on Apr 20.
- Marcus: can you validate the $42k estimate with Finance and confirm whether we can absorb the cost or if we need to pass through a one-time integration fee to affected customers?

I sent the Thu 11am PT invite to everyone — link included in the invite. See you there.

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Partnerships & Alliances
Redwood Inference
